EB5InvestorProgram.title: EB-5 Investor Program
EB5InvestorProgram.subTitle: A pathway to U.S. permanent residency through investment and job creation.
EB5InvestorProgram.overviewText: The EB-5 Investor Program allows eligible investors and their families to obtain U.S. green cards by investing in American businesses that create jobs. Our firm guides you through every step, from investment selection to application and approval.
EB5InvestorProgram.aboutText: The EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program is a U.S. immigrant visa program that provides a path to lawful permanent residency (green card) for foreign nationals who make a qualifying investment in a new commercial enterprise (NCE) that creates the required number of jobs. In 2022, Congress passed the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (RIA), a holistic reform of the EB-5 program, which became effective on March 15, 2022.
EB5InvestorProgram.benefitGreenCard: Pathway to U.S. Green Card for you and your family
EB5InvestorProgram.benefitNoSponsorship: No sponsorship required from an employer or family member
EB5InvestorProgram.benefitFreedom: Freedom to live, work, and study anywhere in the U.S.
EB5InvestorProgram.benefitCitizenship: Potential for U.S. citizenship after five years
EB5InvestorProgram.investmentAmountContent: The EB-5 program requires a minimum investment of $800,000 in a Targeted Employment Area (TEA) or an infrastructure project (a new category under RIA). For other areas, the minimum is $1,050,000. Under RIA, these minimum amounts will be adjusted for inflation every five years.
EB5InvestorProgram.sourceOfFundsContent: EB-5 investors must provide sufficient documentation in their I-526/I-526E petition to demonstrate that the minimum investment funds, plus any administrative fees paid to a regional center, have been obtained or earned through lawful means. Lawful source of funds is combined with lawful path of funds, which means investors must provide documentation showing how the funds were transferred to the NCE in the U.S.
EB5InvestorProgram.jobCreationContent: Each investor must create at least 10 full-time jobs for qualifying U.S. workers within two years of becoming a conditional permanent resident. For regional center projects, jobs can be created through indirect or induced means (e.g., jobs calculated by construction costs using RIMS II or IMPLAN). For direct standalone investments, jobs must be created through direct employment (W-2 employees).
EB5InvestorProgram.atRiskInvestmentContent: To qualify, the EB-5 investor must actually place their capital at risk. The mere intent to invest is not sufficient. There must be a risk of loss and a chance of gain. Any guaranteed return, such as a promise to return a certain amount of capital, interest, or a right of ownership/use of real property, will disqualify the investment as “at risk.”
EB5InvestorProgram.step1Description: Meet with our team to review your goals and eligibility.
EB5InvestorProgram.step2Label: Select investment project and conduct due diligence
EB5InvestorProgram.step2Description: Choose a qualifying project and review all details.
EB5InvestorProgram.step3Label: Invest funds and file I-526 petition
EB5InvestorProgram.step3Description: Transfer funds and submit your application.
EB5InvestorProgram.step4Description: USCIS reviews your petition and supporting documents.
EB5InvestorProgram.step5Description: Receive your conditional green card upon approval.
EB5InvestorProgram.step6Label: File I-829 petition to remove conditions after 2 years
EB5InvestorProgram.step6Description: Submit evidence of job creation and investment.
EB5InvestorProgram.question1: How long does the EB-5 process take?
EB5InvestorProgram.answer1: Processing times vary, but the initial petition can take 1-2 years. The full process to permanent residency may take several years depending on individual circumstances.
EB5InvestorProgram.question2: Can my family members get green cards too?
EB5InvestorProgram.answer2: Yes, your spouse and unmarried children under 21 can be included in your EB-5 application.
EB5InvestorProgram.question3: Do I have to manage the business myself?
EB5InvestorProgram.answer3: No, you do not need to be involved in day-to-day management, but you must be involved in policy formation or as a limited partner.

Immigration.title: Immigration
Immigration.subTitle: The United States is a nation of immigrants. Every year, hundreds of thousands of people from foreign countries immigrate to the U.S. to pursue their American Dream through family, employment, or political asylum.
Immigration.familyBasedImmigrationNote: Issues can arise due to changes in circumstances while petitions are pending (e.g., death of a U.S. citizen, a child turning 21, or divorce).
Immigration.employmentBasedImmigrationNote: Other non-immigrant working visas include H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, O, E-1/2, J, etc. Many holding non-immigrant visas may adjust status to permanent resident. Legal issues such as overstaying or criminal records can affect eligibility.

Immigration.familyPreferenceDescription: Siblings, married children, and permanent residents’ spouses/unmarried children.
Immigration.service2Description: EB-1A, EB-1B, EB-1C, EB-2, EB-3, and EB-5
Immigration.service3Description: Consultation and strategies for L-1A and EB-1C
Immigration.service4Description: Project evaluation, source of funds strategies
Immigration.service5Description: Advance parole, work permits, and more
Immigration.service6Description: National Visa Center and U.S. Embassy processing
Immigration.service8Description: Student visa (F), status changes, citizenship, I-601 waivers
Immigration.question1: What is the difference between a green card and a visa?
Immigration.answer1: A visa allows you to enter and stay in the United States for a specific purpose and period of time, such as tourism, study, or work. A green card (permanent resident card) grants you the right to live and work in the U.S. permanently.
Immigration.question2: How long does it take to process a family-based immigration petition?
Immigration.answer2: Processing times vary depending on the relationship, the applicant’s country of origin, and the specific visa category. Immediate relatives of U.S. citizens generally have shorter wait times, while other categories may experience longer delays due to annual quotas.
Immigration.question3: Can I work in the U.S. while my green card application is pending?
Immigration.answer3: In many cases, you may apply for a work permit (Employment Authorization Document) while your green card application is being processed. Once approved, this permit allows you to work legally in the United States until your application is decided.

BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.title: Business Entities & Corporate Governance
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.subTitle: The right business entity sets the foundation for your company's success, impacting everything from daily operations to liability and growth.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.overviewText: Selecting the right business entity and structure is a critical first step for any startup or growing business. Your choice will impact relationships among partners, daily operations, taxation, capital raising, asset protection, and legal liability. Each entity type, such as sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation (C Corp or S Corp), limited liability company (LLC), joint venture, or nonprofit, offers distinct advantages and considerations. The optimal structure depends on factors like your business’s nature, risk profile, capital needs, ownership, financial goals, and liability concerns. Our experienced legal team will help you navigate these options and choose the most suitable entity to support your business objectives and long-term success.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.entitySelectionTitle: Strategic Guidance on Entity Selection and Jurisdiction
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.entitySelectionDescription: Receive expert advice on choosing the most suitable business entity and jurisdiction—whether domestic, foreign, or offshore—to align with your operational and legal objectives.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.registrationDescription: Benefit from end-to-end support in registering your business entity, ensuring compliance with all regulatory requirements and a smooth setup process.

BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.agreementDraftingDescription: Protect your interests with professionally drafted partnership and joint venture agreements tailored to your business goals and relationships.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.governanceSupportTitle: Ongoing Corporate Governance and Compliance Support
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.governanceSupportDescription: Maintain your company’s good standing with ongoing guidance on corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and best practices for managing legal obligations.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.question1: What factors should I consider when choosing a business entity for my company?
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.answer1: When selecting a business entity, consider your company’s risk profile, tax implications, ownership structure, capital needs, liability concerns, and long-term business goals. Each entity type offers different advantages and legal protections.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.question2: How long does it take to register a new business entity, and what documents are required?
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.answer2: The registration timeline varies by jurisdiction and entity type, but most businesses can be registered within a few days to several weeks. Commonly required documents include articles of incorporation or organization, partnership agreements, and identification for owners or partners.
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.question3: What are the ongoing compliance requirements for corporations and LLCs?
BusinessEntitiesCorporateGovernance.answer3: Corporations and LLCs must maintain good standing by filing annual reports, holding regular meetings, keeping accurate records, and complying with tax and regulatory obligations. Our legal team can help you stay compliant and avoid penalties.

BusinessTransactions.title: Business Transactions
BusinessTransactions.subTitle: Strategic Legal Counsel for Every Stage of Your Business Journey
BusinessTransactions.overviewText: Understanding your rights, obligations, and potential consequences before signing any contract is essential to protecting your business interests. Business agreements often involve complex legal implications that may not be immediately apparent.
BusinessTransactions.aboutText: Our attorneys provide comprehensive legal guidance throughout your entire business lifecycle. We assist with entity formation, due diligence reviews, asset protection strategies, intellectual property safeguarding, contract negotiation and drafting, tax planning, corporate governance, transaction closing, and enforcement. Successful business transactions require counsel with deep expertise across multiple legal disciplines, practical business acumen, strong negotiation skills, and cultural sensitivity. Our team brings this multifaceted experience to every client engagement, ensuring your transactions are structured properly and your interests are protected.
BusinessTransactions.dueDiligenceDescription: Comprehensive investigation and analysis of your target company or asset. We review financial records, contracts, intellectual property, regulatory compliance, potential liabilities, and operational matters to uncover risks and opportunities before you commit.
BusinessTransactions.dueDiligenceWhyItMatters: Thorough due diligence protects you from unexpected liabilities, valuation errors, and deal-breaking issues. It provides the factual foundation for informed negotiation and can save millions by identifying problems before closing.
BusinessTransactions.dueDiligenceWhoNeedsIt: Business buyers, investors, lenders, and companies considering mergers or acquisitions. Essential for any significant business transaction or investment decision.
BusinessTransactions.preNegotiationDescription: Strategic planning sessions to define your objectives, assess leverage points, identify potential deal structures, and develop negotiation tactics. We help you understand your position, anticipate counterparty responses, and establish clear boundaries before entering discussions.
BusinessTransactions.preNegotiationWhyItMatters: Preparation determines negotiation outcomes. A well-crafted strategy helps you secure favorable terms, avoid common pitfalls, and maintain control throughout the process. Knowing your walk-away point prevents costly mistakes driven by emotion.
BusinessTransactions.preNegotiationWhoNeedsIt: Any party entering complex business negotiations, including acquisitions, partnerships, major contracts, or dispute resolutions where significant value is at stake.
BusinessTransactions.negotiationDescription: Direct representation and advocacy during business negotiations. Our attorneys lead or support discussions on your behalf, addressing deal terms, price, warranties, indemnities, closing conditions, and dispute resolution mechanisms while protecting your interests.
BusinessTransactions.negotiationWhyItMatters: Skilled legal representation ensures your business interests are protected while maintaining productive relationships. We balance assertiveness with pragmatism to achieve optimal outcomes without jeopardizing the deal or future business relationships.
BusinessTransactions.negotiationWhoNeedsIt: Companies and individuals negotiating high-stakes transactions, complex contracts, or situations where legal expertise and objective perspective add significant value to the outcome.
BusinessTransactions.corporateGovernanceDescription: Ongoing advisory services for board structure, director duties, shareholder rights, corporate policies, meeting procedures, voting mechanisms, and compliance with corporate formalities. We draft bylaws, operating agreements, and governance policies tailored to your business.
BusinessTransactions.corporateGovernanceWhyItMatters: Proper governance protects against internal disputes, personal liability, and legal challenges. It establishes clear decision-making authority, protects minority interests, and demonstrates professionalism to investors, lenders, and partners.
BusinessTransactions.corporateGovernanceWhoNeedsIt: Corporations, LLCs, and partnerships seeking to establish or improve governance structures, especially growing companies, those with multiple owners, or businesses preparing for investment or sale.
BusinessTransactions.mergersAcquisitionsDescription: Full-service M&A representation from deal structuring through closing. We handle negotiations, due diligence coordination, regulatory filings, purchase agreements, asset or stock transfers, financing arrangements, employee matters, and post-closing integration support.
BusinessTransactions.mergersAcquisitionsWhyItMatters: M&A transactions involve complex legal, financial, and operational considerations with significant risk. Expert guidance ensures deal structure optimization for tax and liability purposes, regulatory compliance, and protection against post-closing disputes.
BusinessTransactions.mergersAcquisitionsWhoNeedsIt: Companies buying or selling businesses, private equity firms, strategic buyers, and business owners planning exits or growth through acquisition.
BusinessTransactions.buySellAgreementsDescription: Drafting and negotiation of shareholder or member buy-sell agreements that govern ownership transfers, valuation methods, triggering events, and purchase obligations. We also craft enforceable non-competition and non-solicitation agreements to protect business interests.
BusinessTransactions.buySellAgreementsWhyItMatters: These agreements prevent costly disputes when owners leave, retire, or divorce. They ensure orderly transitions, protect company value, and maintain business continuity. Well-drafted non-compete clauses protect against unfair competition from former partners or employees.
BusinessTransactions.buySellAgreementsWhoNeedsIt: Multi-owner businesses, professional partnerships, and companies with key employees or executives who have access to confidential information, client relationships, or trade secrets.
BusinessTransactions.stockPurchaseTitle: Stock or LLC Interest Purchase Agreements
BusinessTransactions.stockPurchaseDescription: Preparation and negotiation of comprehensive agreements for the purchase and sale of company ownership interests. We address purchase price, payment terms, representations and warranties, indemnification, closing conditions, escrows, and earn-out provisions.
BusinessTransactions.stockPurchaseWhyItMatters: These agreements define the rights and obligations of all parties, allocate risk, and provide remedies for breaches. Proper documentation prevents misunderstandings and protects both buyers and sellers from future disputes and unexpected liabilities.
BusinessTransactions.stockPurchaseWhoNeedsIt: Buyers and sellers of business ownership interests, whether acquiring control, minority stakes, or exiting partial ownership positions in corporations or LLCs.
BusinessTransactions.partnershipAgreementsDescription: Customized partnership agreements and LLC operating agreements that define ownership percentages, capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management authority, decision-making processes, dispute resolution, and exit procedures for business partners.
BusinessTransactions.partnershipAgreementsWhyItMatters: Clear partnership terms prevent conflicts, protect investments, and ensure business continuity. A well-drafted agreement addresses the inevitable challenges of multi-party ownership and provides mechanisms for resolving disagreements without destroying the business.
BusinessTransactions.partnershipAgreementsWhoNeedsIt: New business ventures with multiple owners, existing partnerships formalizing their relationship, and businesses experiencing partner disagreements due to inadequate or outdated agreements.
BusinessTransactions.ipLicensingDescription: Negotiation and drafting of IP license agreements, assignments, and transfers covering patents, trademarks, copyrights, and proprietary technology. We define scope of use, territories, exclusivity, royalties, quality control, and termination rights.
BusinessTransactions.ipLicensingWhyItMatters: Intellectual property often represents your most valuable business asset. Proper licensing and assignment agreements protect ownership, generate revenue, prevent unauthorized use, and avoid costly litigation over IP rights and usage terms.
BusinessTransactions.ipLicensingWhoNeedsIt: Technology companies, creators, inventors, franchisors, manufacturers, and any business that develops, owns, or uses valuable intellectual property as part of its operations or revenue model.
BusinessTransactions.tradeSecretDescription: Confidentiality agreements, non-disclosure agreements (NDAs), and trade secret protection policies for employees, contractors, and business partners. We identify protectable information, establish security protocols, and create enforceable obligations to maintain secrecy.
BusinessTransactions.tradeSecretWhyItMatters: Trade secrets lose legal protection if not properly safeguarded. Formal agreements establish legal obligations, document confidentiality expectations, and provide remedies for breaches, helping you protect competitive advantages and proprietary information.
BusinessTransactions.tradeSecretWhoNeedsIt: Businesses with valuable proprietary information, client lists, processes, formulas, or know-how; companies sharing sensitive information with partners, vendors, or potential investors; and employers with access to competitor trade secrets.
BusinessTransactions.annualConsultationDescription: Ongoing legal advisory relationship providing proactive guidance on corporate compliance, contract reviews, governance matters, regulatory updates, risk management, and strategic planning. Regular check-ins ensure your business stays legally sound throughout the year.
BusinessTransactions.annualConsultationWhyItMatters: Preventive legal care is more cost-effective than crisis management. Annual consultation helps you avoid problems before they arise, stay compliant with changing laws, and access immediate legal guidance when opportunities or challenges emerge.
BusinessTransactions.annualConsultationWhoNeedsIt: Established businesses seeking a trusted legal advisor for ongoing needs, companies in regulated industries, and organizations preferring proactive legal support over reactive crisis response.
